name: Motor Driven Cycle
description: Indiana's moped and scooter category: a road-legal motor vehicle with a seat, no more than three wheels and a cylinder capacity of 50 cc or less, registered as a motor driven cycle and ridden at 35 mph or less. Its only size limit is that 50 cc cylinder capacity; it sets no power limit for an electric motor. Defined by Indiana Code §9-13-2-104.1, which replaced the former moped (motorized bicycle) category in 2014 (P.L.221-2014) and dropped its over-50 cc Class A in 2022 (P.L.111-2021).

restrictions.rule: A seat or saddle, and no more than three wheels on the ground
A cylinder capacity of 50 cc or less; there's no power or wattage limit for an electric motor

Being registered as a motor driven cycle is part of the definition, and one so registered isn't a motorcycle; one with operable pedals and a motor of 750 W or less that meets an e-bike class is an electric bicycle instead
Built for highway use: meets federal motor vehicle safety standards (49 CFR 571) and Indiana's equipment rules, with a headlamp lit whenever it's ridden
Riders must be 15 or older and carry a driver's license, a learner's permit, or a state ID card with a motor driven cycle endorsement, which takes a knowledge test
Riders and passengers under 18 must wear a DOT motorcycle helmet and protective glasses, goggles or a face shield
Registered with the BMV and carries a motor driven cycle plate; no title or insurance needed, and exempt from the electric vehicle supplemental fee
Can't be ridden faster than 35 mph, or carry a passenger
Kept as far right on the roadway as practicable, except to pass or turn left
Not allowed on interstate highways or sidewalks
